post.description:
Starts a session: signs in with an email address and a password.
Punch checks the password before the transaction; the same answer
comes for an unknown address and a wrong password (lib/punch/docs/auth.md). An
account none of whose addresses is verified yet is refused, with the

post.description:
Creates a user with an email identity and a password, and mails a link
to verify the address (`EmailAdded`). They sign in once they have
followed it: until then nobody has shown that the address is theirs,
and someone else may have typed it (lib/punch/docs/auth.md).
The password is hashed before the transaction opens. The language the
browser asked for becomes the user's.

Billing.Statements.Created.description:
A new statement: its ID alone, since a client's idempotency key keeps
this answer as it is. `Show` has the rest.

Billing.Statements.Detail.description:
A statement as the API shows it to the user who keeps it: `filename` is
decrypted here, and `url` saves the file under a plain name, so the real
one is in no link. `Create` does not answer with this: a client's
idempotency key would keep the name and the link in plaintext.
